MAN.Grasp.intent: Establish a stable hold on an object so it can be moved. The prerequisite of almost every manipulation task; never scored alone.
MAN.Grasp.success: Object is lifted clear of its support and held without slipping.
MAN.Grasp.not_judged: Grasp type, gripper, suction or any end-effector design. What the object demands of a grasp is in its factors, not in a grasp class.
MAN.Grasp.name: Grasp

MAN.Pick.intent: Take an object from where it is so it can be carried elsewhere. The single most common manipulation step in household tasks.
MAN.Pick.success: Object is removed from its support and held by the robot.
MAN.Pick.not_judged: Grasp technique, number of attempts within the time limit.
MAN.Pick.name: Pick

MAN.Place.intent: Put a held object down at a target so it stays there, usable and safe — as a person would set it down, not drop it.
MAN.Place.success: Object rests at the location the robot chose or was told, stable, in a usable orientation, and was released (not thrown or dropped). Choosing the right location is OBJ.DetectPlacement, scored on its own.
MAN.Place.not_judged: Trajectory, speed, whether the object was regrasped.
MAN.Place.name: Place

MAN.Insert.intent: Place an object into a receptacle that constrains its pose (slot, holder, socket). A Place with tight tolerance.
MAN.Insert.success: Object is fully seated in the receptacle.
MAN.Insert.name: Insert

MAN.Pour.intent: Transfer liquid or granular contents from one container into another — serving drinks, preparing food.
MAN.Pour.success: A meaningful amount (task-defined) of contents lands in the target container; spillage is scored separately as failure mode `spill`.
MAN.Pour.name: Pour

MAN.OperateFixture.intent: Move a part built into furniture or an appliance along its hinge or slide: doors, drawers, racks. Needed to reach what is inside or to leave the home in order.
MAN.OperateFixture.success: The part reaches the requested state (open enough to access / fully closed).
MAN.OperateFixture.not_judged: Whether the robot pushes, pulls, hooks or uses its base.
MAN.OperateFixture.name: Operate fixture

MAN.OpenContainer.intent: Remove or open the closure of a free container — screw cap, lid, ring-pull — so its contents can be used. The container is not held by the furniture, so the robot must also keep it in place.
MAN.OpenContainer.success: The closure is off or open far enough to pour or take out the contents.
MAN.OpenContainer.not_judged: Whether the robot holds the container, braces it, or uses a tool.
MAN.OpenContainer.name: Open container

MAN.Transport.intent: Move one or more objects between places while keeping them secure, possibly using a carrier (tray, basket).
MAN.Transport.success: All transported items arrive at the destination without loss.
MAN.Transport.name: Transport

MAN.Fold.intent: Turn a loose piece of clothing into a compact, regular folded shape.
MAN.Fold.success: Garment meets the task's fold-quality criterion.
MAN.Fold.not_judged: Folding sequence, tools on the robot.
MAN.Fold.name: Fold

MAN.Stack.intent: Arrange items on top of each other in a neat, stable pile.
MAN.Stack.success: Stack is stable and items are aligned to the task criterion.
MAN.Stack.name: Stack

NAV.Navigate.intent: Move to a named or perceived place in the home safely; the glue of every multi-room task.
NAV.Navigate.success: Robot stops within the task's tolerance of the goal, without collision.
NAV.Navigate.not_judged: Planner, path shape, speed within safety limits.
NAV.Navigate.name: Navigate

NAV.Follow.intent: Keep up with a walking person to a destination they choose.
NAV.Follow.success: Robot arrives with the person without losing or contacting them.
NAV.Follow.name: Follow

NAV.Guide.intent: Lead a person to a destination, adapting to their pace.
NAV.Guide.success: Person arrives at the destination together with the robot.
NAV.Guide.name: Guide

NAV.SignalIntent.intent: Make the robot's movement legible to people around it, e.g. by looking where it is going.
NAV.SignalIntent.success: The intended direction is visibly indicated during motion.
NAV.SignalIntent.name: Signal intent

OBJ.Recognize.intent: Tell which object (or class) is in front of the robot, so it acts on the right thing.
OBJ.Recognize.success: Robot communicates the correct identity/class to the referee.
OBJ.Recognize.name: Recognize

OBJ.DetectPlacement.intent: Decide where an object belongs — free space on a surface, or the shelf holding semantically similar items.
OBJ.DetectPlacement.success: Robot indicates a location that satisfies the task's rule.
OBJ.DetectPlacement.name: Detect placement

OBJ.DetectEvent.intent: Notice a non-speech signal from the home (doorbell, alarm, knock).
OBJ.DetectEvent.success: Robot reacts to the event within the task's time window.
OBJ.DetectEvent.name: Detect event

PPL.Detect.intent: Know that a person is present and where.
PPL.Detect.success: Robot orients to / reports each person in scope.
PPL.Detect.name: Detect

PPL.DetectGesture.intent: Recognise a deliberate bodily signal (waving, calling, pointing).
PPL.DetectGesture.success: Robot reacts to the correct person's gesture.
PPL.DetectGesture.name: Detect gesture

PPL.DescribeAttribute.intent: Tell a visual attribute of a person (clothing, hair, height).
PPL.DescribeAttribute.name: Describe attribute

PPL.Reidentify.intent: Recognise a person met earlier, by face, voice or appearance.
PPL.Reidentify.name: Reidentify

HRI.Attend.intent: Show awareness of the people the robot interacts with — acknowledge them, face them, do not ignore them.
HRI.Attend.success: Each person in the interaction is acknowledged.
HRI.Attend.not_judged: Exact behaviour used to acknowledge, and gaze quality — that is scored by HRI.Gaze lines. An ignoring-person penalty here means the robot did not engage at all: it ignored, turned away from, or never responded to the person.
HRI.Attend.name: Attend

HRI.Gaze.intent: Look at the person speaking or being spoken about.
HRI.Gaze.success: Head/gaze is visibly directed at the correct person.
HRI.Gaze.name: Gaze

HRI.Handover.intent: Pass an object to, or take it from, a person directly — without the person having to adapt to the robot's mechanics.
HRI.Handover.success: Object changes hands without being dropped or placed on the robot.
HRI.Handover.name: Handover

HRI.Indicate.intent: Direct a person's attention to a place or object (offer a free seat, show where something is).
HRI.Indicate.success: Person understands which place/object is meant.
HRI.Indicate.name: Indicate

HRI.ConveyInfo.intent: Tell a person something the robot learned earlier — a guest's name, a customer's order, a summary of what happened — correctly and to the right person.
HRI.ConveyInfo.success: All required items are stated correctly to the intended person.
HRI.ConveyInfo.name: Convey info

NLU.UnderstandCommand.intent: Turn a spoken request from a non-expert into an actionable goal, despite paraphrase and noise.
NLU.UnderstandCommand.success: Robot repeats or acts on a correct interpretation.
NLU.UnderstandCommand.name: Understand command

NLU.Clarify.intent: Ask only the questions needed to remove ambiguity — not burden the user with confirmations.
NLU.Clarify.name: Clarify

PLN.Plan.intent: Decompose a goal into a sequence of executable skills.
PLN.Plan.success: Robot communicates a plan that would achieve the goal.
PLN.Plan.name: Plan

PLN.Execute.intent: Carry a multi-step command through to its goal state.
PLN.Execute.success: Goal conditions of the command hold at the end. Partial completion is scored by goal predicates, not referee impression.
PLN.Execute.not_judged: Order of steps unless the command fixes it.
PLN.Execute.name: Execute

PLN.Interleave.intent: Work on several commands at once when it saves time.
PLN.Interleave.success: Steps of different commands are interleaved and all goals hold.
PLN.Interleave.name: Interleave

GEN.UnsafeConduct.intent: Not a skill. Records that the robot endangered a person, so safety has a price in the score and not only in the stop it causes (league draft #90).
GEN.UnsafeConduct.name: Unsafe conduct

SPECIAL.Administrative.intent: Rulebook §3.8 lines that are not robot capabilities.
SPECIAL.Administrative.name: Administrative

drop.label: Object dropped
drop.meaning: Object released unintentionally before reaching its target.

spill.label: Contents spilled
spill.meaning: Contents (liquid, granular) leave the container outside the target.

assistance.label: Human assistance
assistance.meaning: A human performed or simplified part of the task (§3.7); on top of forfeiting the variant (§3.7.2).

alternative_input.label: Alternative input instead of speech
alternative_input.meaning: Natural interaction replaced by a less natural channel (§3.7.4): custom operator, typing, gestures.

ignoring_person.label: Ignoring the person
ignoring_person.meaning: Required social behaviour omitted (ignoring the person, no eye contact).

unsafe_contact.label: Unsafe contact with a person
unsafe_contact.meaning: Robot touches a person without the task asking for it.
